title: Conflicts of interest, other people's money and honest records

say: Conflicts of interest, other people's money, and honest records.
This is the video for module two of Ethics and Accountability at Work.
A conflict of interest exists when your personal interest, or that of someone close to you, could influence a decision you make for your employer, customers or group.
Having a conflict is not wrong in itself. Hiding it, or deciding anyway, is where the harm begins.

cards.d: Your interest and your duty clash right now, like interviewing your niece for a job.
They could clash in future, like your husband's company bidding for a contract you will judge.
Others could reasonably believe your judgement is affected, even if it is not.

say: For example, Halima chairs a 40-member farming cooperative near Kaduna. They want 100 bags of fertiliser, and one of three quotes is from her cousin's agro shop.

say: The cousin's shop is lowest, and the minutes record the three totals and the reason. Nobody can fairly accuse Halima of favouritism.

say: Good money controls are not an insult to honest people. They protect honest people, because when money goes missing, clear records show exactly what happened.

panel.heading: Five controls that protect you
items: Count cash together and both sign

say: Give a receipt for every payment in, and ask for one for every payment out.

panel.heading: Five controls that protect you
items: Count cash together and both sign

say: The person who collects money should not be the only one who records and checks it.

panel.heading: Five controls that protect you
items: Count cash together and both sign

say: Withdrawals from a group account need two authorised people.

panel.heading: Five controls that protect you
items: Count cash together and both sign

say: Count cash in front of a second person, and both sign.

panel.heading: Five controls that protect you
items: Count cash together and both sign

say: And match your records to the bank or mobile money statement every month.

say: Never mix group or employer money with your own, and never borrow from the float, even for one day. Money misuse rarely starts big. It starts with a small borrowing that goes unnoticed.

say: Bank cash quickly. And remember, an SMS or a screenshot is not proof of payment. Fraudsters fake them. Confirm the credit inside your own banking or mobile money app before you release goods or record a payment.

say: Everyone makes recording errors. What matters is how you correct them. On paper, draw a single line through the wrong entry, so it can still be read. No correction fluid, and never tear out pages.

say: For example, Aisha, an admin officer in Abuja, sent a client an invoice for 450,000 naira instead of 540,000. She told her manager the same morning.
The client had already approved the wrong amount.
She had prepared a supplementary invoice for 90,000 naira, with a polite note and the delivery note attached.
And she now compares every invoice total with the delivery note before sending. The company recovered the money, and her manager saw someone who owns errors quickly.
Your practice. List your interests, mark each as actual, potential or perceived, and write one declaration.
Reconcile one month of money you handle and explain every difference. Then check ten recent entries in one of your records, and correct any errors openly.
